newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its two-hour session on Monday 0.03 percent higher compared with the previous session, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 435.79 points compared with 435.65 points on Friday.
"Despite the bourse index slight change, market activity was flat due largely to the blue-chip stocks stable price," a market analyst said.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, remained stable at 499 dirhams compared with the previous session.
ONA has diversified stakes in more than 100 companies and a capitalisation of more than 8.3 billion dirhams.
The conglomerate's agro-industry subsidiaries, Centrale Laitiere, Lesieur, which made substantial gains last week were not traded on Monday, the analyst added.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, a very liquid stock, remained unchanged at 685 dirhams.
The Cyprus-based Capital Intelligence specialist bank rating service said on Monday it had raised the long-term rating of Morocco's Banque Commerciale du Maroc to BBB+ (BBB plus) from BBB.
In a statement sent to Reuters, it said the short-term rating was re-affirmed at A-2 "and a stable outlook has been assigned".
Capital Intelligence added: "In recent years, the bank has adopted a strategy of diversification with the creation of several associated companies which specialise in a variety of financial services.
With total assets of $3.6 billion at end 1995, BCM is Morocco's third largest bank, the rating service said.
Traded volume on the official market was 8.8 million dirhams from 51.8 million dirhams on Friday.
